notes: REAL VENDOR: d-Matrix (d-matrix.ai). Set to 'asic-other' because the schema enum does not include 'd-matrix'. d-Matrix Corsair is a digital in-memory compute inference accelerator that entered full production in June 2026, with volume shipping to priority customers. The architecture uses chiplet design with 256 MB SRAM per die, 2,048 MAC arrays, and digital in-memory computing to eliminate the memory wall. The key innovation is the two-tier memory system: 2 GB of on-chip integrated Performance Memory at 150 TB/s (an order of magnitude above HBM) plus up to 256 GB of off-chip Capacity Memory. The card is a full-height full-length PCIe 5.0 x16 card with CXL 2.0 support. The compute is block-scaled integer (MXINT8/MXINT4), not floating-point — this is deliberately aimed at weight-only quantization for LLM inference. The white paper states peak dense compute of 2,400 TFLOPS for MXINT8 and 9,600 TFLOPS for MXINT4 equivalent. TDP is not published at the card level; the white paper mentions <5W per die but the card contains multiple dies. The product brief mentions 1 pJ/MAC-class efficiency. Corsair is aimed at datacenter inference for LLMs and is NOT a training chip. The company was founded by Sudeep Bhoja and Sid Sheth, both former Wave Computing executives. Process node is 7nm. The chiplet approach allows scaling to larger systems via die-to-die interconnects.
